about: Phase 0 baseline for the performance campaign, measured on the LIVE deployed install (M1 Pro, 17 GB, 2026-07-29). Every later claim in this campaign must diff against this file. Read-only measurements plus one lightweight socket round-trip each; no benchmark loops (see the hazard note).
hazard_note: Generating load on this machine CRASHES the inference server. Two concurrent Core ML conversions and, separately, one op=generate each triggered a Metal command-buffer timeout (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorTimeout, exit -6, launchd restart). Five such timeouts in this log, one of them timestamped 2026-07-28 17:17 which PREDATES this session's changes. Mechanism is memory pressure, see below. CONSEQUENCE: benchmark-heavy phases must not run against the live install.

memory.why_this_is_first: This reordered the whole campaign. Shaving milliseconds off IPC is meaningless while 93% of the inference server's writable memory is swapped out.
memory.honesty: DARWIN is NOT the only pressure. Top RSS at measurement time was Comet (1.6 GB) and Claude helpers (~1.7 GB combined), plus this session's own subagents and cargo builds. DARWIN's share is the 5.35 GB footprint above.
memory.ATTRIBUTION_CORRECTION: Re-measured after killing this session's leftover subagent processes: swap went UP (12.8 -> 13.4 GB) while DARWIN's footprint held steady at 5208 MB / peak 6979 MB. So the swap pressure is substantially THIS SESSION'S OWN TOOLING (Claude helpers ~1.9 GB plus concurrent audit agents), not DARWIN. HONEST CONSEQUENCE: 'the machine is swapping' is NOT on its own a justification for reclaiming memory from DARWIN - 5.2 GB for a 4B LLM plus STT, TTS and a retrieval stack is not obviously wrong on a 17 GB machine. Memory work here has to be justified as GENUINE WASTE (the spec-decode draft model was: a measured loss AND unreachable), not as relief for pressure an outside process is causing.

startup.CORRECTION: An earlier draft of this file said TTS dominates startup at 37.3 s of 63 s. That was measured on a CONTENDED boot - the Core ML fast-graph rebuild was converting in the background during it, and its MIL progress bars are interleaved in that very log line. On a clean boot TTS preload is 4.7 s and the TTS WEIGHT load is 0.3-0.5 s. The real dominator is the KV prompt-cache prefills.
startup.finding: The two KV prompt-cache prefills (persona 2063 tokens, classifier 869 tokens) are ~33 s of the ~63 s. TTS weights are 0.5 s, which makes TTS a CHEAP parking candidate rather than a startup problem. The draft model's 2.2 s goes with speculative decoding.
startup.lesson: Measure on an UNCONTENDED boot. A background conversion inflated one stage 8x and I recorded it as the headline finding.

ipc_overhead.why: The ANE work made the graph fast enough that framing now dominates short ops.
ipc_overhead.finding: A short embed costs 1.84 ms at the graph and 6.61 ms over the unix socket with JSON framing - the framing costs more than the model. Rerank shows 5.9x through the wire vs 9.70x at the graph, same dilution.

speculative_decoding.verdict: REMOVED - it was a measured loss AND unreachable
speculative_decoding.source: inference/benchmarks/baseline_m1_pro.json, results.speculative (already committed; this phase only had to read it)
speculative_decoding.cached_path_reason: mlx_lm rejects a draft_model together with a prompt_cache (IndexError); DARWIN's persona and classifier paths are KV-cached, so the production path always ran normal decode
speculative_decoding.note: It shipped ON with the draft checkpoint pre-downloaded by the installer, so a 16 GB machine that swaps was holding a 335 MB model the generate path could never use.

next: Memory work first (idle model parking, TTS residency given the opener bank, and whether the GPU-timeout crash class is a memory-pressure symptom), then re-measure before touching IPC or models.

kv_prompt_caches.computed_from: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-4bit config.json: 36 layers, 8 kv heads, head_dim 128, fp16 K+V
kv_prompt_caches.capability: mlx_lm 0.31.3 exposes save_prompt_cache / load_prompt_cache / trim_prompt_cache, so these COULD be persisted to disk and loaded instead of re-prefilled each boot
kv_prompt_caches.unresolved: persisting saves STARTUP, not memory (the cache is resident either way). Its real safety argument is that it removes ~33 s of GPU prefill at boot - the most fragile moment, and where the Metal command-buffer timeouts occur. A stale cache silently paired with a changed persona would be a correctness hazard, so it would need a strict fingerprint (model id + quant + prompt hash + mlx_lm version).

confirmed_waste_found.method: 73-agent audit over resident models, caches and startup work; every finding double-refuted

1_prefill_materialized_891MB_of_discarde.what: Both KV prompt-cache prefills ran the FULL model and mx.eval'd the logits, forcing the tied lm_head projection of every prefix position out to vocab_size 151,936.
1_prefill_materialized_891MB_of_discarde.fix: evaluate [c.state for c in cache] instead - mlx_lm's own prefill pattern. MLX is lazy, so the projection never enters the graph.
1_prefill_materialized_891MB_of_discarde.proven: miniature model with the same shape: peak 470.4 MB with eval(logits) vs 159.3 MB with eval(cache), a 311.2 MB saving exactly equal to the logits tensor. Cache is bit-identical either way.
1_prefill_materialized_891MB_of_discarde.why_it_matters: the transient landed during boot, which is both the peak-memory moment (7694 MB peak vs 5352 MB steady) and where the Metal command-buffer timeouts occur

2_live_config_still_had_speculative_on.what: the repo fix was committed but the LIVE ~/Library/Application Support/DARWIN/config/darwin.toml still carried speculative=true + the draft model, so 335 MB and 2.2 s were still being paid at every boot
2_live_config_still_had_speculative_on.resolution: lands on the next redeploy; verify install.sh overwrites the deployed config rather than preserving it

3_installer_copied_2.5GB_of_benchmark_sc.what: scratch-bench/ is gitignored with zero tracked files and is never read by the runtime, but was not in EXCLUDE_DIRS, so every ./install.sh --yes rsynced 2.5 GB into the install home - almost all of it an ane-probe/ tree with its OWN hf-cache holding a SECOND full copy of the 4B checkpoint

4_rejected_checkpoints_still_on_disk.what: 7.32 GiB of candidate models that were downloaded, LOST their eval, and were never cleaned up - TTS candidates rejected by the RTF gate (csm-1b-8bit, orpheus variants, snac vocoder), classifier candidates rejected by the accuracy gate (Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama-3.2-1B), and whisper-large-v3-turbo rejected by the STT comparison
4_rejected_checkpoints_still_on_disk.status: REPORTED ONLY - deleting user files is destructive and was not done without asking

after_phase0_fixes.measured: 2026-07-29 boot, machine load ~14 (a runaway browser was holding ~2.7 cores; the BEFORE column was taken under comparable contention)

honest_cost.coreml_embedder: 13.2 -> 14.8 s and reranker 3.9 -> 6.9 s. This is the ANE fast path loading TWO graphs instead of one - a real startup cost paid for a 10.7x/9.70x per-predict win, and it belongs in the ledger.
honest_cost.net: the startup saving is real but smaller than the prefill numbers alone suggest, because the Core ML stages grew

after_phase0_fixes.what_did_it: removing the discarded vocab projection from all three prefills (891 MB at boot plus ~1.2 GB per large consolidate), and dropping the speculative draft model that was both a measured 27% decode loss and unreachable on the KV-cached path

phase1_ipc_premise.the_claim_i_made: a short embed costs 6.61 ms over the wire vs 1.84 ms at the graph, so ~4.8 ms is IPC overhead worth optimizing (connection pooling + binary framing)
what_was_wrong_with_it: The 6.61 ms was measured with a FRESH socket per call. I assumed the daemon did the same. It does not - daemon/src/inference.rs caches `conn` and ensure_connected() only connects when it is None. So connection pooling was already there and could not be the win.
Re-measured properly: POOLED p50 8.48 ms vs FRESH p50 8.65 ms - statistically the same. Unix-socket connect is not the cost.

The remaining figure is not trustworthy either. p50 8.48 ms with min 4.03 and p90 11.78 is contention variance, not a fixed cost, and it was taken at machine load ~14 with a runaway browser holding ~2.7 cores. The 1.84 ms graph number it is being differenced against was measured on a quiet machine.
phase1_ipc_premise.what_can_be_said: best-case overhead is about 2.2 ms (min 4.03 minus the 1.84 graph cost), part of which is tokenization - real work, not overhead. That is a far smaller prize than 4.8 ms.
phase1_ipc_premise.verdict: DEFER, not a NO-GO. The IPC premise cannot be validated on this machine in its current state; the measurement is dominated by contention rather than by the thing the optimization would remove. Re-measure on a quiet machine before building anything.
phase1_ipc_premise.meta: This is the THIRD measurement this session corrupted by machine contention (after the 37.3 s TTS figure and the 43 s startup stage). Every remaining campaign phase - retrieval tuning, model-refresh evals - is measurement-dependent, so the machine's load is the blocking issue for the campaign, not any code.

RESOLVED_ON_A_QUIET_MACHINE.context: the user closed the runaway browser; load fell 43 -> 8 and swap 13.4 -> 3.46 GB, so these numbers are finally trustworthy
RESOLVED_ON_A_QUIET_MACHINE.the_decisive_observation: the LONG embed costs 19.33 ms on the wire against a 19.65 ms graph cost - wire overhead is within noise of zero. A fixed multi-millisecond IPC cost would have made it ~25 ms.
RESOLVED_ON_A_QUIET_MACHINE.verdict: NO-GO, not a defer. The entire IPC + dispatch + framing path is 0.22 ms of a 4.08 ms request (5%). Binary framing would target the 0.105 ms of JSON; connection pooling already exists in daemon/src/inference.rs. There is no prize here.
RESOLVED_ON_A_QUIET_MACHINE.what_this_retires: the 'IPC fast path' half of Phase 1. The remaining Phase 1 items (TTS first-audio streaming, an ANE-native STT evaluation) are untouched by this and still stand on their own.
